messages.content: The Twin Cities conference just changed again. Wednesday closing session now runs until 11:45, and the St. Paul campus-partner visit moved to 2:15. I’m still on the 7:35 MSP-SLC flight. Can you sanity-check the whole Wednesday sequence with checkout and luggage?

Yes. One thing matters for flight reliability: how long is the St. Paul visit expected to run? If it ends around 3:45 or 4:00, the 7:35 flight still looks comfortable. If they expect you there past 4:30, I’d look at a backup.
They have it as 2:15 to 3:45, maybe 4:00 if the conversation runs. I can store my bag at the Residence Inn and go straight to MSP afterward.

Keep the 7:35 return. Suggested plan: breakfast at the hotel, check out and leave your bag with the front desk before the closing session, return to the hotel by about 12:05, quick lunch or coffee nearby from 12:10 to 12:35, rideshare to St. Paul around 12:40, and arrive roughly 1:10 to 1:25. That leaves a very safe cushion before 2:15.
Would you still store the suitcase downtown instead of carrying it to St. Paul?

Yes. Storing it downtown is cleaner unless the front desk suddenly says they cannot hold it. Carrying the suitcase through the campus visit would make lunch and the meeting awkward, and the extra hotel stop still fits the timeline.
What if the visit runs late? I don’t want to be watching the clock the whole time.

Set a hard departure from St. Paul at 4:30. Typical rideshare time from St. Paul to MSP is about 20 to 30 minutes; with pickup wait and traffic, a 5:15 to 5:30 airport arrival is still a healthy buffer for a 7:35 departure. If they are not wrapping by 4:15, politely flag that you need to leave for your flight.
Okay. Add the seat/check-in and food note so I don’t forget.

Calendar notes: Tuesday evening, check in for the MSP-SLC flight and confirm the window seat is still assigned; if the seat map shifted, pick any standard window that is available. Wednesday, eat a real hotel breakfast, pack a snack, check out and tag luggage before the session, grab a quick lunch downtown before St. Paul, then rideshare St. Paul to MSP with a 5:30 airport target. No flight change needed unless the St. Paul visit becomes an evening or dinner event.

messages.content: Switching from conference travel to kid logistics: we have a mid-July Boise-area tournament weekend. We’ll drive from Salt Lake after work Friday and stay two nights. Games may be split between Nampa and west Boise. I need a practical hotel area shortlist with two queens, parking, breakfast, and somewhere to get dinner after a late drive.

I can narrow that. What are the exact dates, how many people, and how early Saturday could start? The Nampa versus Meridian versus west Boise choice really changes if there is an 8:00 a.m. report time.
July 18 to 20, four of us, no pets. First game could be 8:00, but the schedule is not posted yet. We’d probably leave SLC around 4:30, so Boise arrival is more like 10:15 or 10:30.

Given the uncertainty, I’d compare three zones. Nampa is best if Saturday starts early there: shortest morning drive and often easier parking, but fewer late dinner choices. Meridian is the balanced option: usually 15 to 25 minutes to Nampa or west Boise, with better food access. West Boise is best for Friday-night restaurants and could be good if Sunday shifts that way, but it is the least forgiving for an early Nampa start.
Can you make that into a shortlist rather than just the areas?

Shortlist to check live inventory: 1) Hampton Inn & Suites Nampa/Idaho Center area, two-queen refundable room, free parking, breakfast often early enough for tournament mornings, closest to Nampa venues. 2) A Hampton, Homewood, or Tru in Meridian near Eagle Road, two queens if available, free parking, breakfast, best compromise location. 3) Home2 Suites Boise West or Hyatt Place Boise/Towne Square area, good dinner access and breakfast, but longer Saturday drive if Nampa gets the early slot.
The kids will be starving by then, and I don’t want to rely on a hotel pantry at 10:30.

That leans Meridian or west Boise. Around Eagle Road and west Boise you’ll have more late fast-casual options than Nampa. If you choose Nampa, I’d plan dinner in Twin Falls or Burley before the last stretch, or choose a specific Nampa restaurant and confirm the kitchen closing time before you leave Salt Lake.
Saturday morning matters too. If Nampa gets the 8:00 slot, how bad is west Boise?

It is doable but less relaxed. West Boise to a Nampa venue can be 25 to 35 minutes early on a weekend morning, so you might leave the hotel around 7:00 for a 7:35 or 7:40 arrival. Meridian is more forgiving, and Nampa is obviously easiest. Breakfast hours are the pinch: some hotels start at 6:30 on weekends, some later, so verify the actual Saturday time.
Let’s assume I can hold one now. Would you hold Meridian?

Yes, if there is a cancellable two-queen Meridian room with free parking and breakfast starting by 6:30, that is the best temporary hold while the schedule is unknown. If Meridian is too expensive or only nonrefundable, I’d hold west Boise over Nampa for now because of Friday food and possible Sunday flexibility, then switch to Nampa if the posted schedule confirms an early Nampa game.
What exact things should I check before entering the card?

Check the cancellation deadline in Mountain Time, that the room is specifically two queens and non-smoking, free self-parking, breakfast hours for both Saturday and Sunday, whether late arrival after 10:30 can be noted, and the drive times to the Nampa and west Boise venues. I’d also ask whether a Sunday late checkout can be requested at check-in, since brackets can run oddly.

messages.content: Tournament schedule posted, and of course the hotel inventory changed. Saturday starts in Nampa with a 7:45 arrival. Sunday bracket may move to Meridian. The Meridian hotel no longer has a cancellable two-queen room. Nampa Hampton has a refundable two-queen, breakfast at 6:00. West Boise Home2 is also refundable, breakfast at 6:30, and better restaurants. Which one should I book?

Book the Nampa Hampton. With a firm 7:45 Nampa arrival, the earlier breakfast and short morning drive are worth more than Friday-night restaurant convenience. West Boise is workable, but you’d need a very quick breakfast and a departure around 7:00.
We’ll probably reach Nampa around 10:15 if traffic is okay. Are there enough food options?

There are fewer than west Boise, but it is manageable if you plan it. I would either eat in Twin Falls or Burley before the last leg, or pick a Nampa spot in advance and confirm the kitchen closing time. I would not wait until arrival to decide with hungry teenagers in the car.
What cancellation and parking details should I save?

Save the local-time cancellation deadline, the refundable rate name, taxes and fees, confirmation number, and exact room type. Parking should be free self-parking, but capture that line on the confirmation. Add a late-arrival note because you may check in after 10:00.
And Sunday if the bracket moves to Meridian?
From the Nampa/Idaho Center area to common Meridian fields, budget 20 to 30 minutes, or 35 if teams are all moving at once. That is a reasonable trade for making Saturday morning much safer.
Okay, I’ll book Nampa. Should I ask for late checkout now or at check-in?

Book the cancellable two-queen Nampa room now. Put the requests in now and repeat them at check-in: late arrival Friday, quiet room if available, and Sunday late checkout, ideally noon or 1:00. Calendar: breakfast opens 6:00 Saturday, leave the hotel by 7:25 for the 7:45 arrival, pack snacks Friday night, and recheck the Sunday bracket before breakfast.
